list.title: Communic Flow
list.descProject: Communic Flow is a multi-level organizational dashboard designed to modernize institutional communication. It connects organizations, their affiliates, and members through a centralized platform offering information management, role-based access control, event planning, claim management, real-time messaging, and Power BI reporting. Initially developed for the National Chamber of the Pharmaceutical Industry (CNIP), the application addresses real needs for coordination, transparency, and rapid information flow across complex ecosystems.

description.title: Main Features
points: Centralized institutional information across organizations and affiliates
Complete hierarchical structure: Super Administrator → Organizations → Members
Advanced claim management: creation, tracking, and responses
Real-time messaging with Socket.IO (groups and individual chats)
Event planning and scheduling
Advanced user, role, and permission management
Management of organizations and their affiliates
Power BI integration for interactive analytics and decision-making

Automated continuous integration for both frontend and backend
Application containerization using Docker with image storage in Nexus Repository
Automated code quality analysis with SonarQube and strict Quality Gates
Security and vulnerability scanning using OWASP Dependency-Check
Application and pipeline monitoring via Prometheus
Performance metrics visualization using Grafana
Automated deployment pipeline to the VPS with artifact management

list.title: Communic Flow — Version 2
list.descProject: Communic Flow v2 represents the redesigned and upgraded version of the multi-level organizational platform, now rebuilt with a modern microservices architecture. Messaging is fully isolated as an independent service powered by GraphQL and Redis for inter-service communication. The authentication system has been enhanced with secure HTTP-Only cookies, Google OAuth 2.0, Cloudflare Turnstile to block spam, and a complete two-factor authentication flow. Company creation is optimized with automated VIES validation for EU companies and ZIP-based address autofill. Backend security has been significantly reinforced, and real-time messaging performance has been improved to support future features such as voice and video calling.

citation.name: Janet Williams
citation.citation: Computer science is more than just lines of code. It's the expression of creativity, problem-solving, and building a digital future.

blogList.title: Design Patterns in Practice: SOLID, Testable Architecture

desc.title: Why patterns — and when not to
desc.description: Use patterns to reduce coupling and improve clarity, not as cargo‑cult. Prefer simple composition unless a pattern measurably improves testability or changeability.

desc.title: SOLID and composition first
desc.description: Apply SRP and DIP to keep modules small and replaceable. Compose behaviors via interfaces; isolate I/O at boundaries to enable pure, unit‑testable cores.

desc.title: Dependency Inversion with DI
desc.description: Depend on abstractions. Inject collaborators (factories, strategies, adapters) to swap implementations in tests and production without touching consumers.

desc.title: Selecting patterns pragmatically
desc.description: Prefer Strategy over if/else trees, Adapter to integrate legacy APIs, Factory to centralize creation with validation and caching. Avoid global Singletons.

desc.title: Smells to avoid
desc.description: God objects, deep inheritance, over‑abstraction and premature patterning. Measure impact: fewer defects, simpler diffs, faster reviews.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Patterns are tools. Start with clear boundaries, enforce interfaces, and document decisions. Fewer surprises, easier onboarding, better uptime.

blogList.title: Angular Performance: Measurable Wins in the Real World

desc.title: Profile before you tune
desc.description: Use Chrome Performance, Lighthouse, and Angular DevTools to locate slow change detection, heavy zones, and chatty network calls.

desc.title: Change detection + rendering
desc.description: Adopt OnPush + `trackBy` for lists, prefer pure pipes, memoize derived state, and split views with `*ngIf` to defer cost.

desc.title: Network and data flow
desc.description: Batch HTTP requests, cache with RxJS `shareReplay`, debounce user input, and stream incremental data for faster First Interaction.

desc.title: Bundles and delivery
desc.description: Lazy‑load routes, leverage standalone components, audit with `source-map-explorer`, and use image compression + HTTP/2.

desc.title: Guardrails
desc.description: Set CI budgets, watch Core Web Vitals, and fail builds on regressions. Performance is a product requirement, not an afterthought.

blogList.title: Modern React: Hooks, Performance and Clean State

desc.title: Design for simplicity
desc.description: Prefer local state with hooks, lift state only when needed, and co‑locate logic with UI. Small components, clear props contracts.

desc.title: Rendering performance
desc.description: Use `memo`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` judiciously; key lists correctly; virtualize large tables; split bundles with dynamic import.

desc.title: Data fetching patterns
desc.description: Stale‑while‑revalidate with SWR/React Query, optimistic updates, and error boundaries for resilient UX.

desc.title: Testing and accessibility
desc.description: Test with React Testing Library (user‑centric). Ship ARIA‑aware components and verify with axe and keyboard navigation.

desc.title: Maintainability
desc.description: Type with TypeScript, enforce ESLint + Prettier, and document props and invariants.

blogList.title: Practical DevOps: CI/CD, Observability, and Reliability

desc.title: Trunk‑based CI/CD
desc.description: Short‑lived branches, automated tests, and canary releases keep deploys boring. Enforce quality gates with coverage and lint checks.

desc.title: Infrastructure as Code
desc.description: Provision reproducibly with Terraform/Pulumi. Version everything; review changes like code; tag releases and roll back fast.

desc.title: Observability that matters
desc.description: Define SLOs, collect RED/USE metrics, add structured logs with correlation IDs, and trace user journeys.

desc.title: Security in the pipeline
desc.description: SAST/DAST, image scanning, SBOMs, and signed artifacts. Least privilege for runners and secrets management.

desc.title: Runbooks and readiness
desc.description: Health checks, graceful shutdown, and documented incident playbooks. Practice failure injection to build confidence.

blogList.title: Effective TypeScript: Types that Scale with Teams

desc.title: Start strict, stay strict
desc.description: Enable `strict` and incremental builds. Prefer explicit types at boundaries; let inference work inside functions.

desc.title: Modeling with unions
desc.description: Use discriminated unions over flags. Encode invariants in the type system and eliminate whole classes of runtime checks.

desc.title: APIs and contracts
desc.description: Define DTOs and use `zod`/`io-ts` for runtime validation. Generate types from schemas to avoid drift.

desc.title: Utilities and generics
desc.description: Leverage utility types (`Partial`, `Pick`, `Extract`) and thoughtful generics for reusable, readable APIs.

desc.title: Tooling
desc.description: ESLint + Prettier + TS path aliases; enforce no‑any, no‑implicit‑any, and unused checks in CI.

blogList.title: Portfolio SEO: Technical Wins that Recruiters Notice

desc.title: Foundation
desc.description: Unique titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, sitemap.xml and robots.txt. Add JSON‑LD (Person, Project) for rich results.

desc.title: Speed and vitals
desc.description: Optimize images, preconnect critical origins, lazy‑load below‑the‑fold, and monitor LCP/CLS/INP in production.

desc.title: Content that signals expertise
desc.description: Write case studies with problem → approach → measurable outcome. Link to code, demos, and metrics.

desc.title: Internationalization
desc.description: Use `hreflang` and consistent slugs across locales. Keep translations accurate and in sync.

desc.title: Tracking and iteration
desc.description: Set up GA4 + Search Console; review queries and improve pages that already rank on page 2.

blogList.title: GraphQL vs REST: Choose by Constraints, Not Hype

desc.title: When REST wins
desc.description: Simple resources, CDN caching, and long‑lived clients. Version via new representations; keep endpoints stable.

desc.title: When GraphQL shines
desc.description: Mobile/low‑latency apps and complex graphs. Fetch exactly what you need; evolve schemas without breaking clients.

desc.title: Performance reality
desc.description: Guard against N+1 with dataloaders; enforce pagination and depth limits; cache persisted queries.

desc.title: Operational concerns
desc.description: Observability, timeouts, and error budgets matter more than style. Document with OpenAPI/SDL and provide examples.

desc.title: Decision rubric
desc.description: Pick the simplest option that meets SLAs. Hybrid backends are common; measure, don’t guess.

blogList.title: Docker Done Right: Small Images, Fast Deploys

desc.title: Build for production
desc.description: Use multi‑stage builds, pin versions, and minimize layers. Add healthchecks and non‑root users.

desc.title: Smaller, safer images
desc.description: Leverage distroless/alpine when appropriate, `.dockerignore` aggressively, and scan images in CI.

desc.title: Local dev ergonomics
desc.description: Compose for services, bind mounts for hot reload, and named volumes for state.

desc.title: Operational tips
desc.description: Expose minimal ports, set resource limits, and emit structured logs. Document run commands for on‑call.

blogList.title: Testing that Prevents Incidents: A Practical Pyramid

desc.title: Test the contract
desc.description: Favor fast unit tests and contract tests at service boundaries. Mock only what you own.

desc.title: Integration > E2E for most cases
desc.description: A few critical E2E flows are enough. Focus on integration tests for realistic coverage with maintainable speed.

desc.title: Data and determinism
desc.description: Use seed data, freeze time, and isolate external effects. Flaky tests destroy trust and velocity.

desc.title: Coverage as a guide
desc.description: Track mutation coverage where possible and require thresholds in CI; quality over raw percentages.

blogList.title: PWAs that Feel Native: Offline‑First by Design

desc.title: Core capabilities
desc.description: Add installability (Web App Manifest), offline caching, and background sync. Respect user prompts; don’t hijack.

desc.title: Caching strategy
desc.description: Precache shell, runtime cache data, and version aggressively. Plan for invalidation and migrations.

desc.title: UX considerations
desc.description: Design explicit offline states, queue writes, and surface sync status. Keep interactions responsive under poor networks.

desc.title: Measuring success
desc.description: Track install rate, offline sessions served, and crash‑free users. Iterate based on real usage.

blogList.title: Secure Authentication: Cookies, OAuth2 + PKCE, 2FA, Turnstile

desc.title: Why this matters
desc.description: Most auth incidents stem from session handling and weak flows, not cryptography. Use a pragmatic design that is secure, scalable, and user‑friendly.

desc.title: Cookie sessions over localStorage
desc.description: Prefer HTTP‑only, Secure, SameSite cookies with short TTL and rotation. Avoid storing tokens in localStorage to reduce XSS token theft risk.

desc.title: OAuth 2.0 + PKCE
desc.description: Use Authorization Code with PKCE for third‑party login (e.g., Google). Enforce exact redirect URIs, narrow scopes, and validate the state parameter.

desc.title: Add Two‑Factor Authentication
desc.description: Start with TOTP and backup codes; add WebAuthn for phishing resistance. Require step‑up auth for sensitive actions (admin, payouts).

desc.title: Block automated abuse
desc.description: Protect signup/login and recovery forms with Cloudflare Turnstile; always verify on the server. Combine with rate limiting and anomaly detection.

desc.title: Production checklist
desc.description: CSRF protection, session rotation, token revocation, rate limits, device/IP reputation, structured logging without secrets, and security tests in CI (OWASP ASVS).

blogList.title: Real‑Time Messaging with GraphQL Subscriptions + Redis

desc.title: Why isolate messaging
desc.description: Real‑time workloads have unique scaling, ordering, and reliability needs. A dedicated microservice improves performance and team velocity.

desc.title: Core architecture
desc.description: GraphQL over HTTP for queries/mutations; Subscriptions (WebSockets) for realtime. Redis Pub/Sub for live fanout; Redis Streams + DB for durable history.

desc.title: Pub/Sub vs Streams
desc.description: Pub/Sub is low latency and ephemeral; Streams are ordered and durable with backpressure and replay. Use both: Streams for persistence, Pub/Sub for online fanout.

desc.title: Backpressure and ordering
desc.description: Persist first, ack after durable write. Use Stream IDs for per‑conversation order and idempotency keys to prevent duplicates.

desc.title: Security and abuse controls
desc.description: Authorize on subscribe/publish, rate‑limit sends, encrypt in transit/at rest, and apply quotas per user/org.
